text:
## 1) Detection logic

### Sigma: suspicious `schtasks.exe` creation

```yaml
title: Suspicious Windows Scheduled Task Creation via schtasks.exe
id: 2f5d8b6a-2c24-4d1a-9f23-scheduled-task-suspicious-create
status: experimental
description: Detects suspicious scheduled task creation using schtasks.exe with potentially malicious execution targets or persistence patterns.
author: your-org
date: 2026/06/02
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_schtasks_create:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/Create'
      - '-Create'

  suspicious_tr:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'powershell'
      - 'pwsh'
      - 'cmd.exe'
      - 'wscript'
      - 'cscript'
      - 'mshta'
      - 'rundll32'
      - 'regsvr32'
      - 'wmic'
      - 'bitsadmin'
      - 'certutil'
      - 'curl'
      - 'wget'
      - 'python'
      - 'perl'
      - 'node'
      - 'java'
      - 'msiexec'

  suspicious_locations:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '\Users\Public\'
      - '\AppData\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\Windows\Tasks\'
      - '\Recycle.Bin\'
      - '\\127.0.0.1\'
      - '\\localhost\'
      - '\\'

  suspicious_flags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -enc'
      - ' -encodedcommand'
      - ' -nop'
      - ' -noprofile'
      - ' -w hidden'
      - ' -windowstyle hidden'
      - 'bypass'
      - 'unrestricted'
      - 'downloadstring'
      - 'invoke-webrequest'
      - 'iex '
      - 'frombase64string'
      - '/SC MINUTE'
      - '/SC ONLOGON'
      - '/SC ONSTART'
      - '/RU SYSTEM'
      - '/RL HIGHEST'

  condition: selection_schtasks_create and 1 of suspicious_*
fields:
  - UtcTime
  - User
  - Image
  - ParentImage
  - CommandLine
  - ParentCommandLine
  - CurrentDirectory
  - Computer
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software updaters
  - Enterprise management tools
  - Backup agents
  - EDR/AV scheduled maintenance tasks
  - Admin scripts creating scheduled tasks
level: high
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1053.005
```

---

### Sigma: Windows Security Event ID 4698 task creation

```yaml
title: Suspicious Windows Scheduled Task Registration
id: 9b81066c-6b7c-43e2-8af1-task-registration-suspicious
status: experimental
description: Detects suspicious scheduled task registration from Security Event ID 4698 based on task content.
author: your-org
date: 2026/06/02
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4698

  suspicious_commands:
    TaskContent|contains:
      - '<Command>powershell.exe</Command>'
      - '<Command>pwsh.exe</Command>'
      - '<Command>cmd.exe</Command>'
      - '<Command>wscript.exe</Command>'
      - '<Command>cscript.exe</Command>'
      - '<Command>mshta.exe</Command>'
      - '<Command>rundll32.exe</Command>'
      - '<Command>regsvr32.exe</Command>'
      - '<Command>wmic.exe</Command>'
      - '<Command>bitsadmin.exe</Command>'
      - '<Command>certutil.exe</Command>'
      - '<Command>msiexec.exe</Command>'

  suspicious_args:
    TaskContent|contains:
      - '-enc'
      - '-encodedcommand'
      - '-nop'
      - '-noprofile'
      - '-windowstyle hidden'
      - '-w hidden'
      - 'ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
      - 'DownloadString'
      - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
      - 'Invoke-Expression'
      - 'FromBase64String'
      - '\Users\Public\'
      - '\AppData\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - '\\'

  suspicious_schedule:
    TaskContent|contains:
      - '<Interval>PT1M</Interval>'
      - '<Interval>PT5M</Interval>'
      - '<LogonTrigger>'
      - '<BootTrigger>'

  condition: selection and 1 of suspicious_*
fields:
  - Computer
  - SubjectUserName
  - SubjectDomainName
  - TaskName
  - TaskContent
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate updater or monitoring tasks
  - Administrative automation
  - Configuration management tooling
level: high
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1053.005
```

---

### Splunk SPL: process creation, Event ID 4688

```spl
index=windows sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4688
| eval cmd=coalesce(CommandLine, Process_Command_Line)
| eval image=coalesce(NewProcessName, Image)
| where like(lower(image), "%\\schtasks.exe")
| where match(lower(cmd), "(^|\\s)(/create|-create)(\\s|$)")
| eval suspicious_reason=mvappend(
    if(match(lower(cmd), "powershell|pwsh|cmd\\.exe|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|wmic|bitsadmin|certutil|msiexec|curl|wget"), "LOLBIN_or_script_interpreter", null()),
    if(match(lower(cmd), "\\\\users\\\\public\\\\|\\\\appdata\\\\|\\\\temp\\\\|\\\\programdata\\\\|\\\\windows\\\\tasks\\\\|\\\\recycle\\.bin\\\\"), "suspicious_path", null()),
    if(match(lower(cmd), "-enc|-encodedcommand|-nop|-noprofile|-w hidden|-windowstyle hidden|executionpolicy\\s+bypass|downloadstring|invoke-webrequest|iex|frombase64string"), "suspicious_powershell_or_obfuscation", null()),
    if(match(lower(cmd), "/sc\\s+minute|/sc\\s+onlogon|/sc\\s+onstart|/ru\\s+system|/rl\\s+highest"), "suspicious_schedule_or_privilege", null()),
    if(match(lower(cmd), "http://|https://|\\\\\\\\"), "network_reference", null())
)
| where mvcount(suspicious_reason) > 0
| table _time host user ParentProcessName image cmd suspicious_reason
```

---

### Splunk SPL: scheduled task registration, Event ID 4698

```spl
index=windows sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4698
| eval task_content=coalesce(TaskContent, Message)
| eval task_name=coalesce(TaskName, Task_Name)
| eval lc=lower(task_content)
| eval suspicious_reason=mvappend(
    if(match(lc, "<command>.*(powershell|pwsh|cmd\\.exe|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|wmic|bitsadmin|certutil|msiexec).*?</command>"), "suspicious_command", null()),
    if(match(lc, "-enc|-encodedcommand|-nop|-noprofile|-w hidden|-windowstyle hidden|executionpolicy bypass|downloadstring|invoke-webrequest|invoke-expression|frombase64string"), "suspicious_args_or_obfuscation", null()),
    if(match(lc, "\\\\users\\\\public\\\\|\\\\appdata\\\\|\\\\temp\\\\|\\\\programdata\\\\|\\\\windows\\\\tasks\\\\"), "suspicious_path", null()),
    if(match(lc, "http://|https://|\\\\\\\\"), "network_or_unc_reference", null()),
    if(match(lc, "<logontrigger>|<boottrigger>|<interval>pt1m</interval>|<interval>pt5m</interval>|<interval>pt10m</interval>"), "suspicious_trigger_or_frequency", null())
)
| where mvcount(suspicious_reason) > 0
| table _time host SubjectUserName SubjectDomainName task_name suspicious_reason task_content
```

---

## 2) Suspicious command-line patterns

High-signal scheduled task creation patterns include:

### Suspicious task creation syntax

```text
schtasks /Create
schtasks.exe /Create
schtasks -Create
```

### Suspicious schedule frequency or trigger

```text
/SC MINUTE
/MO 1
/MO 5
/MO 10
/SC ONLOGON
/SC ONSTART
/SC DAILY /ST 00:00
```

Frequent minute-based execution is often used for persistence or retry logic.

### Elevated execution

```text
/RU SYSTEM
/RL HIGHEST
/RU "NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM"
```

### Suspicious task action

```text
/TR "powershell.exe ..."
/TR "cmd.exe /c ..."
/TR "wscript.exe ..."
/TR "cscript.exe ..."
/TR "mshta.exe ..."
/TR "rundll32.exe ..."
/TR "regsvr32.exe ..."
/TR "wmic.exe ..."
/TR "bitsadmin.exe ..."
/TR "certutil.exe ..."
/TR "msiexec.exe ..."
```

### PowerShell abuse indicators

```text
-ExecutionPolicy Bypass
-ep bypass
-EncodedCommand
-enc
-NoProfile
-nop
-WindowStyle Hidden
-w hidden
DownloadString
Invoke-WebRequest
iwr
Invoke-Expression
iex
FromBase64String
```

### Suspicious file locations

```text
C:\Users\Public\
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\
C:\Windows\Temp\
C:\Temp\
C:\ProgramData\
C:\Windows\Tasks\
C:\$Recycle.Bin\
```

### Network or remote payload references

```text
http://
https://
\\server\share\
\\IP-address\share\
```

### Masquerading names

```text
AdobeUpdateTask
ChromeUpdateTask
GoogleUpdate
OneDriveUpdate
WindowsUpdate
MicrosoftEdgeUpdate
SecurityHealth
SystemUpdate
```

These names are not malicious by themselves, but they are suspicious when paired with unusual paths, interpreters, or unsigned payloads.

---

## 3) MITRE ATT&CK mapping

Primary mapping:

| Tactic | Technique | ID |
|---|---|---|
| Persistence | Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task | `T1053.005` |
| Privilege Escalation | Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task | `T1053.005` |
| Execution | Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell | `T1059.001` |
| Execution | Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell | `T1059.003` |

Possible additional mappings depending on observed command:

| Behavior | Technique |
|---|---|
| Use of `rundll32.exe`, `regsvr32.exe`, `mshta.exe` | `T1218` - System Binary Proxy Execution |
| Use of encoded PowerShell | `T1027` - Obfuscated Files or Information |
| Downloading payloads over HTTP/S | `T1105` - Ingress Tool Transfer |
| Execution from user-writable paths | Supports persistence/execution tradecraft |
| Masquerading as updater tasks | `T1036` - Masquerading |
| Running as SYSTEM or highest privileges | Privilege escalation via scheduled task abuse |

---

## 4) Likely false positives

Common benign sources include:

1. **Software updaters**
   - Adobe, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Java, Zoom, Teams, Firefox, OneDrive.

2. **Enterprise management tools**
   - SCCM/MECM, Intune, Tanium, BigFix, PDQ Deploy, Kaseya, NinjaOne, ConnectWise, LANDesk/Ivanti.

3. **Backup and monitoring agents**
   - Veeam, Acronis, Datto, Splunk UF scripts, vulnerability scanners.

4. **Security tools**
   - EDR, antivirus, compliance agents, hardening scripts.

5. **Admin automation**
   - GPO startup/logon scripts.
   - Helpdesk-created remediation tasks.
   - One-time maintenance tasks.

6. **Legitimate PowerShell automation**
   - Especially if your environment uses PowerShell for patching, inventory, or compliance.

---

## 5) Tuning and enrichment recommendations

### Tuning ideas

1. **Allowlist known-good task names**
   - Example: known Google, Adobe, Edge, and enterprise management tasks.
   - Be cautious: attackers often mimic these names.

2. **Allowlist expected parent processes**
   - Examples:
     - `C:\Windows\System32\mmc.exe`
     - `C:\Windows\System32\taskschd.msc`
     - known deployment agent paths.

3. **Allowlist trusted task paths**
   - Vendor-specific scheduled task folders.
   - Example:
     - `\Microsoft\Windows\`
     - `\GoogleUpdateTaskMachineCore`
   - But validate action path and signature too.

4. **Prioritize user-writable execution paths**
   - Increase severity if task action points to:
     - `C:\Users\Public\`
     - `%AppData%`
     - `%Temp%`
     - `%ProgramData%`

5. **Prioritize risky interpreters**
   - `powershell.exe`
   - `cmd.exe`
   - `wscript.exe`
   - `mshta.exe`
   - `rundll32.exe`
   - `regsvr32.exe`

6. **Prioritize encoded or hidden execution**
   - `-EncodedCommand`
   - `-WindowStyle Hidden`
   - `ExecutionPolicy Bypass`

7. **Correlate Event ID 4688 and 4698**
   - 4688 shows `schtasks.exe` execution.
   - 4698 shows the registered task content.
   - Alert confidence is higher when both are present from the same host/user/time window.

8. **Add risk scoring**
   - Example scoring:
     - `+30` scheduled task created.
     - `+30` PowerShell/cmd action.
     - `+25` user-writable path.
     - `+25` encoded or hidden PowerShell.
     - `+20` runs as SYSTEM or highest.
     - `+20` network download.
     - Alert when score `>=50`.

### Useful enrichment fields

Enrich the alert with:

- Hostname.
- User and domain.
- User type: standard, local admin, domain admin, service account.
- Parent process.
- Process integrity level.
- Full command line.
- Task name.
- Task XML/content.
- Task action command and arguments.
- Task trigger.
- Task principal/run-as account.
- File path referenced by the task.
- File hash of the referenced executable/script.
- Digital signature status.
- File creation time.
- Reputation of domain/IP if network reference exists.
- Recent logon events for the user.
- Recent privilege changes.
- EDR process tree.
- Whether the task still exists.

---

## 6) Recommended investigation steps

When the alert fires:

### 1. Review the created task

On the endpoint:

```cmd
schtasks /Query /TN "AdobeUpdateTask" /V /FO LIST
```

Or with PowerShell:

```powershell
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName "AdobeUpdateTask" | Format-List *
Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName "AdobeUpdateTask"
```

Check:

- Task name.
- Task path.
- Author.
- Description.
- Action command.
- Arguments.
- Trigger.
- Run-as user.
- Whether it runs with highest privileges.

---

### 2. Inspect the task action payload

For the example:

```text
powershell.exe -File C:\Users\Public\update.ps1
```

Investigate:

```powershell
Get-Item "C:\Users\Public\update.ps1" | Format-List *
Get-FileHash "C:\Users\Public\update.ps1"
Get-AuthenticodeSignature "C:\Users\Public\update.ps1"
```

Open the script in a safe analysis environment and look for:

- Download cradles.
- Base64.
- `Invoke-Expression`.
- Credential theft.
- Recon commands.
- C2 URLs or IPs.
- Payload staging.

---

### 3. Build a process timeline

Look around the task creation time:

- Parent process of `schtasks.exe`.
- User that launched it.
- Previous commands from the same user.
- Subsequent execution of the task.
- Network connections from the payload process.

Useful event sources:

- Security `4688`.
- Security `4698`, `4702`, `4699`.
- Sysmon Event ID `1` process creation.
- Sysmon Event ID `3` network connection.
- Sysmon Event ID `11` file creation.
- PowerShell `4103`, `4104`.
- Task Scheduler Operational logs:
  - `Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational`
  - Event IDs `106`, `140`, `141`, `200`, `201`.

---

### 4. Determine whether the user action was legitimate

Ask:

- Is the user an administrator?
- Was there a change ticket?
- Was this task deployed by a known management tool?
- Has this user created scheduled tasks before?
- Was the logon interactive, remote, or service-based?
- Did the source IP match expected admin workstations?

---

### 5. Check for persistence and lateral movement

Search enterprise-wide for:

- Same task name.
- Same script name.
- Same file hash.
- Same command line.
- Same URL/IP.
- Same parent process behavior.

Example Splunk search:

```spl
index=windows
("AdobeUpdateTask" OR "C:\\Users\\Public\\update.ps1")
| table _time host user EventCode Image CommandLine TaskName TaskContent
```
